mainEntity.name: What can go wrong during a whole-house interior renovation?

acceptedAnswer.text: The main risks are hidden damage, budget creep, and delays from material shortages or design changes. Whole-house interior renovations often uncover outdated wiring, plumbing problems, uneven framing, or moisture damage once walls and floors are opened. Another common issue is scope drift: adding upgrades after the plan is set can quickly raise costs and extend the timeline. A detailed contract, contingency budget, and upfront decisions reduce most of the pain.
